segments.expected: The Board combed the Hunt's bags back at the gate on the timber pond, as the Clerk had said it would, from four until after six.
segments.transcript: The board combed the hunts to dash back at the gate on the timber pond, as the clerk had said it would, from four until after six. A vote held fifteen, nine, six, no board tin, twenty-six, after Dusselboyt through nine spent. Tellen Lyle's ward gone and his remark without self-exoneration. McClark's patent claim lawful work on three-nine spent. To Clark's patent claim without self-exoneration. The clerk's patent claim without next year mun sitere, no unseldeter. Kellan Lyle's ward gone and his remark without self-exoneration. The clerk's patent claim without next year mun setere, non fifty, no four. Pint one five held six-point-two-six, after zero-point-three-nine spent. Movaak the timber-titting sextus-clern, to tamper one Lyle's ward gone and his remark without self-exoneration. To Clark's patent claim lawful work on three-nine-stead, mesopot-nine sitians. Gnome sex-hands.

segments.expected: Every four came in off the Longshore with its bags, and every bag went on the long table under the mast, and a clerk in grey held a comb over it, and another clerk wrote down what the comb said. The queue went back along the boards and round the end of the Graving's wall. Nobody talked much in it. The word had gone along the causeway and along the Mole and into the town long before any of them came in, and the queue had heard it, and it stood with its bags at its feet and waited.

segments.expected: "I heard. On the causeway. Lyle."
segments.transcript: I heard, on the causeway, Lyle.

segments.expected: "A door." Kellan looked at the boards. "Her ward. Gone, not shut. She held a boom against a shed rung on Carrow's word, and the lodger came out of the pill's mouth like an eel, and Treen called run, and she didn't. I cut it on the mud. I was too late." He said it flatly, the way he did sums. "Bray wrote a remark against me. A dram off Halden on the mark. And our second line was half set when I left it, and at the slack a part of our second rung went past the purse. Bray put that one down to the pill, not to me. I'd have put it to me." He shrugged. "We were combed at five. Eight and two, after shares and the remark. Pettit says he'd have gone himself."

segments.expected: She had thought, all the way up Tar Lane, that she would not say I told you. She had decided it on the causeway, and again at the bottom of the lane, and again at the door. It had been easy to decide. It was harder to sit on a bench beside the girl she had told, twice, and not have it in her mouth.

segments.expected: "It's for a hand," said Kiva. "That's what's written on it. In two books, under two names. For a hand. Not for a bank, a floor, a crossing or a sale." She made herself go on. "It's Seven's word. It's my captain's name and mine. If it were wanted, I'd have to go to my four and to the Order, and say it was wanted, and ask."

segments.expected: The first bag. The rung off the near post, the short one, cut at fourteen minutes past twelve and shut in the slack. Kiva had hauled it. One fathom. Two fathom. Three.

segments.expected: "Trace," said the clerk. He looked up for the first time. "Under trace on the seventh. Clean." He looked at the bag, and at the comb, and at them. "Twelve drams and six-tenths. Clean."

segments.expected: "That's what Penhale said. This morning, when the upper one leaned before a gust." Kiva looked at the sheets on the counter. "I don't know that it heard. I know it moved first. So on the coast the far edge isn't when the tide turns. It's when the thing decides to. Whoever has the far edge can't watch the water for it. They have to watch the thing. The far end of it. All the way through the slack, even when the slack's holding." She was quiet for a moment. "And a stow's a sleeve. It's got two ends. The book's for a sheet."
